p1: King Solomon wrote, “A soft answer turns away anger. But hurting words stir up anger.”
When someone feels hot and mad, gentle words help cool them down. Hurting words make the mad feeling grow bigger.
Solomon also wrote, “Kind words are like a honeycomb, sweet to the soul.”
p2: Bees keep their honey in a honeycomb. Long ago, honey was one of the sweetest treats people had. So kind words taste sweet to the heart. Jesus said He is “meek and lowly in heart,” gentle and kind.
Your words can be sweet like honey too. Tomorrow, when someone is upset, try a soft, gentle answer.
old: Wise Solomon knew that the words we say are very powerful. They can make a heart happy or a heart hurt.
“A soft, kind answer makes angry feelings go away,” Solomon taught. “But mean, grumpy words just make things worse.”
Imagine two friends. One shouts, “You broke it!” — and everyone gets upset. But if that friend says softly, “It’s okay, let’s fix it together,” the mad feelings melt like ice in the sun.
Soft words are gentle words. Kind words are healing words. They help everyone feel calm and loved.
Heavenly Father can help you choose soft, kind words — even when you feel a little grumpy. Gentle words make the whole world happier.
